newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana voters approve major gambling initiative.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana voters approve major gambling initiative.

text.p: A last-minute multi- million-dollar advertising blitz paid off for big gaming interests in Louisiana as New Orleans voters overwhelmingly approved keeping the stalled land-based casino.
The 15 riverboat casinos scattered around the state also won easy approval from local voters.
The ballot initiative gave voters in each parish the authority to keep or boot out any of three forms of legalized gambling already there.

Returns were incomplete in parish-by-parish elections on video poker, an industry staggering under multiple federal corruption indictments of Louisiana public officials and convictions of mob figures. It appeared Wednesday that at least 26 of the state's 64 parishes would ban vido poker.
Louisiana's horseracing, state-wide lottery and off-track betting industries were not affected by the vote.

Construction was halted on Harrah's Jazz casino, a massive structure bordering the French Quarter, and a temporary casino was abruptly closed last November when the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection from creditors.

In a bid to bolster support for the New Orleans casino, Harrah's Jazz officials Monday announced a $50 million bankruptcy reorganization plan through which it will pay 100 percent of the $14 million in claims by unsecured creditors and construction contractors. The rest will go to the big construction companies on the development.
Officials had said the plan would not be finalized until voters decided whether to keep the casino. The casino was approved by 67 percent of New Orleans voters.
The detailed reorganization plan was to be presented in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Orleans Wednesday.
In parishes where voters rejected video poker, operators will have until mid-1999 to eliminate the machines.
